16 consecutive quarters of positive leasing spreads; SNO pipeline $90–140M+; new leases 9% above renewals
Deleveraging roadmap: $6.6B → ~$4.5B debt by 2029–2030, targeting ~6x ND/EBITDA via asset sales

key_debate.street: High leverage (8.2x vs SPG 5.7x, SKT 5.4x), tenant bankruptcies (Forever 21, Claire's) signal structural decline

thesis_points: P/AFFO compressed -28% over 3 years despite AFFO/share growing +2.24% — fundamental valuation disconnect vs structural durability
Churn inflection: Sprint (~$55M, hard stop ~2026), DISH/EchoStar (~$25M, clears 2027–28), then clean organic growth at 5–6%
Brazil structural opportunity: 58% fewer towers per 100K people vs US; legally binding 5G buildout obligations through 2029
ROIC improved 4.7% → 8.9% (2020–2025), best among tower peers; revenue +35% vs CCI -27% in same period
MLA structure locks in 3% annual domestic escalators + amendment fees on every equipment upgrade ($5–10K each)
46,328 towers across 13 countries; 1.8 tenants/tower domestic (vs CCI 2.4x EU 2.1x) = significant colocation runway

key_debate.street: Carrier consolidation churn (Sprint, DISH) suppresses organic growth; Brazilian FX and macro headwinds; Q4 guidance miss signals execution risk
key_debate.our_view: Churn is front-loaded and quantified — Sprint hard stop ~2026, DISH clears 2027–28. Post-churn organic growth re-accelerates to 5%+. Brazil upside is not in consensus

overview.narrative:
Healthcare REITs dominated the tape Tuesday, surging 2.37% on average as the sector's best session in weeks was headlined by Sabra Healthcare's 10.20% spike—likely tied to favorable skilled nursing reimbursement signals or portfolio activity. Diversified Healthcare Trust added 5.93%, confirming broad-based strength across the care continuum. Hospitality followed at +1.62%, led by Summit Hotel Properties' 3.54% gain amid resilient summer travel data. On the flip side, Towers were the clear laggard at -1.64%, with all three major names—SBAC (-2.83%), CCI (-2.53%), and AMT (-2.20%)—selling off in unison, suggesting a duration-driven move as rate expectations firmed.

The ILPT +7.23% outlier in an otherwise modest Industrial tape (+0.78%) points to idiosyncratic catalysts, possibly refinancing progress or asset sale news, rather than sector beta. Meanwhile, IIPR's -1.69% decline kept Industrial gains capped. The Housing weakness (-0.52%) and Retail's muted +0.33% print suggest the consumer-sensitive cohort is treading water, with Simon Property's -0.61% dip notable given its bellwether status.

Positioning into Wednesday favors continued Healthcare momentum, particularly if SBRA's catalyst gets confirmed in filings. Tower shorts may have further room to run if the 10-year holds its move higher. We'd fade the ILPT spike absent fundamental clarity and look for Hospitality continuation above today's levels.

Tower REITs struggled as the session's worst performer, declining 1.64% despite the broader positive trend across the sector.
